description: Stage 5 syncs the execution branch with origin in _fetch_execution_branch (apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/flow/calibrate_sync.py), which calls fetch_base once. When that single git fetch hits a transient SSH, keychain or network failure and refs/remotes/origin/<branch> already exists locally, Stage 5 aborts at once with CalibrationSyncError; a resume 1.4 minutes later, with no host change, fetched and calibrated cleanly. Stage 5 therefore fails for a reason that clears by itself within seconds.
goal: _fetch_execution_branch retries the origin fetch a bounded number of times with a short backoff (three attempts over about 10 to 15 seconds in total) on HostRemoteError before it gives up, and a transient failure on the first attempt that succeeds on a retry no longer fails Stage 5. After the attempts are exhausted the existing behaviour is unchanged: CalibrationSyncError when a local origin ref exists and pushing is enabled, otherwise the existing warning. Each retry is logged in one line through context.log. The retry helper lives in a new small module so that calibrate_sync.py stays within its current module line budget. The module line budgets are frozen: do not edit holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json or any budget-check script, and keep every touched module within its current budget.
rationale: A seconds-long network or SSH hiccup should cost a few seconds of backoff, not a halted stage and a manual resume cycle.
acceptance_criteria: A HostRemoteError on the first fetch followed by a success on a later attempt lets sync_execution_ref complete without raising CalibrationSyncError, and one log line names each retry.
A HostRemoteError on every attempt keeps the existing outcome: CalibrationSyncError when refs/remotes/origin/<branch> exists and skip_push is false, otherwise the existing warning and no raise.
The number of attempts is three, the total backoff stays at or below 15 seconds, and the tests patch the sleep so they take no real time.
The public names of calibrate_sync.py are unchanged; no other source file changes.
The new test file uses fakes or a real temporary git repository, fails on the old code and passes on the new.
The module budgets file and every budget-check script are untouched and every touched module stays within its current line budget.
uv run pytest passes for the new test file and tests/test_calibrate_sync.py.
